import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from datetime import datetime

# Read the data
data = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# Set style
sns.set_palette("husl")

# 1. Sales by Product (Top Left)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
product_sales = data.groupby('product')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=True)
product_sales.plot(kind='barh', ax=ax1, color='steelblue')
ax1.set_title('Total Sales by Product', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
ax1.set_ylabel('Product')

# 2. Sales by Age Group (Top Middle)
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
age_sales = data.groupby('customer_age_group')['total'].sum()
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis", len(age_sales))
ax2.pie(age_sales, labels=age_sales.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=colors)
ax2.set_title('Sales Distribution by Age Group', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 3. Payment Method Distribution (Top Right)
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
payment_counts = data['payment_method'].value_counts()
ax3.bar(payment_counts.index, payment_counts.values, color=['coral', 'lightblue'])
ax3.set_title('Payment Method Usage', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Payment Method')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')

# 4. Sales by Time of Day (Middle Left - Spanning 2 columns)
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
data['hour'] = pd.to_datetime(data['time'], format='%H:%M').dt.hour
hourly_sales = data.groupby('hour')['total'].sum()
ax4.plot(hourly_sales.index, hourly_sales.values, marker='o', linewidth=2, markersize=8, color='darkgreen')
ax4.fill_between(hourly_sales.index, hourly_sales.values, alpha=0.3, color='lightgreen')
ax4.set_title('Sales by Hour of Day', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Hour')
ax4.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 5. Takeaway vs Dine-in (Middle Right)
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
takeaway_data = data['is_takeaway'].map({1: 'Takeaway', 0: 'Dine-in'})
takeaway_counts = takeaway_data.value_counts()
colors = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff']
ax5.bar(takeaway_counts.index, takeaway_counts.values, color=colors)
ax5.set_title('Takeaway vs Dine-in Orders', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_ylabel('Count')

# 6. Average Price by Size (Bottom Left)
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
size_order = ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large']
size_price = data.groupby('size')['price'].mean().reindex(size_order)
ax6.bar(size_price.index, size_price.values, color=['#ffd700', '#ff8c00', '#ff4500'])
ax6.set_title('Average Price by Size', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Size')
ax6.set_ylabel('Average Price ($)')

# 7. Quantity Distribution (Bottom Middle)
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
quantity_counts = data['quantity'].value_counts().sort_index()
ax7.bar(quantity_counts.index, quantity_counts.values, color='mediumpurple')
ax7.set_title('Quantity per Order Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Quantity')
ax7.set_ylabel('Count')

# 8. Total Sales Summary (Bottom Right)
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax8.axis('off')
total_revenue = data['total'].sum()
total_orders = len(data)
avg_order = data['total'].mean()
summary_text = f"Summary Statistics\n\n" \
               f"Total Revenue: ${total_revenue:.2f}\n" \
               f"Total Orders: {total_orders}\n" \
               f"Average Order: ${avg_order:.2f}\n" \
               f"Most Popular: {data['product'].mode()[0]}\n" \
               f"Top Age Group: {data['customer_age_group'].mode()[0]}"
ax8.text(0.5, 0.5, summary_text, ha='center', va='center', 
         fontsize=11, bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='wheat', alpha=0.5),
         family='monospace')

# Main title
fig.suptitle('Coffee Shop Sales Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
